No owner salary is deducted. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Automated QoE & cash reconciliation; Shared HoldCo back-office workflows; key risks: Hidden liabilities; Customer attrition; Debt-service coverage; regulatory notes: Review employment, tax, licenses, lender covenants and transaction disclosures.; track ids: track_1; track_2; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; Grey-Zone Growth & Traffic Arbitrage; plays: id: distressed_asset_recovery; track id: track_1; name: Distressed Asset Recovery; mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.; inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers; Unclaimed property & judgment dockets; Surplus auction manifests; workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances; Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value; Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts; metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case; Claim approval rate; Days from filing to disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold; trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules; impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle; detection metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance; fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required; id: expired_chrome_extension_acquisitions; track id: track_2; name: Dormant Chrome Extension & Shopify App Roll-Up / Monetization Flip; mechanism: Scan the Chrome Web Store, WordPress Plugin Directory, and Shopify App Store for high-install (10,000–250,000 active users), 4.5+-star free utilities neglected by solo developers, acquire them at 1–2x potential annual cashflow, and introduce clean freemium Pro tiers or opt-in contextual partner offers.; inputs: Chrome Web Store / Shopify / WP plugin scraper filtering by active installs, rating, & last-updated date (>12 months); Asset Purchase Agreement (APA) & Chrome Web Store developer-account transfer checklist; Freemium Stripe checkout SDK + non-intrusive opt-in partner recommendation module; workflow: Identify utility extensions and micro-apps with strong organic weekly installs and zero monetization whose solo creator has not pushed an update in 12–24 months; Acquire the codebase, store listing, and domain for $3,000–$35,000 with an escrowed transfer through the official developer console; Ship a Manifest V3 maintenance update first to build user trust, then grandfather existing free features while adding a $7–$19/mo Pro power-user tier or explicit opt-in partner deals; metrics: Acquisition payback period (target 2–5 months); Free-to-Pro conversion rate (1.5–4%) + monthly ARPU per 1,000 WAU; Post-acquisition review rating stability (>=4.4 stars) and uninstall rate (<3%); platform risks: failure mode: Chrome Web Store malware/policy takedown or mass 1-star user revolt after acquisition; trigger: Injecting silent background adware/tracking scripts post-acquisition or locking previously free core features behind a sudden paywall; impact: Permanent Chrome Web Store removal and total write-off of acquisition capital; detection metric: Zero CWS permission-scope expansion without user opt-in and daily 1-star review velocity monitor; fallback: Never inject hidden tracking or background ad scripts; keep existing permissions narrow, grandfather all legacy free features, and monetize strictly via additive Pro workflows; id: chapter11_trade_claim_convenience_class_rollup; track id: track_1; name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups; mechanism: Purchase documented small trade claims below risk-adjusted expected plan distributions, accounting for objections, assignment procedures, and plan rules that may prohibit claim splitting or aggregation benefits.; inputs: Bankruptcy schedules E/F and claims register; Invoices, payment history, and assignment documents; Proposed plan classification and distribution waterfall; workflow: 1. Reconcile scheduled trade creditors with filed claims and supporting invoices; 2. Model recoveries under plan amendments, objections, setoffs, and convenience-class eligibility; 3. Buy eligible claims through documented assignments and complete required transfer notices; 4. Monitor objections and confirmation, then reconcile distributions to each acquired claim; metrics: Purchase discount to risk-adjusted recovery; Allowed claim value versus purchased face value; Realized return and days to distribution; platform risks: failure mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion; trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims; impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss; detection metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio; fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries; id: aged_shelf_corp_tradeline_credit_stacking; track id: track_1; name: Aged Shelf-Corp Reinstatement, Primary Tradeline & 0%-APR Corporate Credit Stacking; mechanism: Compare reinstated entities and genuine business credit facilities for working-capital financing; entity age is not operating history, and promotional APR economics require accurate underwriting and repayment capacity.; inputs: Entity filings, beneficial ownership, and liability searches; Verified operating financials and genuine supplier tradelines; Lender eligibility, promotional APR, fee, and guarantee terms; workflow: 1. Audit the entity's ownership, tax liabilities, and reinstatement requirements; 2. Disclose acquisition and actual operating history; establish only genuine paid supplier accounts; 3. Compare lender-approved applications with full debt disclosure and consolidated exposure limits; 4. Fund documented business expenses and repay before promotional expiry using cash-flow reserves; metrics: Effective borrowing cost including fees; Debt service coverage under post-promotion APR; Utilization and days to promotional expiry; platform risks: failure mode: Credit withdrawal or unaffordable repricing; trigger: Misstated operating history, undisclosed debt, or expired promotional terms; impact: Account closure, accelerated repayment, and guarantee exposure; detection metric: Underwriting discrepancies and stressed repayment coverage; fallback: Halt applications, correct disclosures, and use a transparent term facility or reduce financed spending; id: ferc_grid_interconnection_queue_land_speculation; track id: track_1; name: FERC / ISO Substation Interconnection Queue & Powered-Land Option Flipping; mechanism: Overlay public interconnection queues with land-use and substation data to option potentially useful sites, treating queue position and nearby infrastructure as signals rather than guaranteed deliverable power.; inputs: ISO and utility interconnection queues and study results; Parcel zoning, transmission corridors, and substation maps; Utility service estimates and developer site requirements; workflow: 1. Match queue activity and infrastructure constraints to suitable parcels; 2. Verify site control requirements, zoning, environmental limits, and utility capacity assumptions; 3. Negotiate assignable diligence-contingent options within capped carrying-cost budgets; 4. Assign approved options to qualified developers with explicit disclosure of unresolved power and study conditions; metrics: Option cost per qualified developable acre; Utility-validated capacity versus marketed capacity; Net assignment proceeds after study and option costs; platform risks: failure mode: Queue withdrawal or prohibitive network upgrade cost; trigger: Restudy, milestone failure, or capacity estimate unsupported by utility commitments; impact: Option expiry and unrecoverable diligence spending; detection metric: Study cost revisions and unresolved interconnection milestones; fallback: Let contingent options lapse or reposition land for independently viable uses without claiming secured power; id: wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine; track id: track_1; name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine; mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.; inputs: Consented hiring records, Form 8850 responses, and payroll hours; Research project evidence and qualified expense ledgers; State workforce certification procedures and tax-year credit and fee rules; workflow: 1. Confirm WOTC authorization for each hire date and complete required prescreening by the job-offer date; 2. Submit Form 8850 and required supporting forms within the applicable 28-day deadline and track state certification and qualifying hours; 3. Separately document Section 41 qualifying research and expenses, reconciling wage overlap and applicable deduction adjustments with a tax professional; 4. Obtain employer and preparer approval before filing, retain audit support, and collect permitted fees without guaranteeing credits; metrics: Timely WOTC certification submission rate; Substantiated credits realized by the employer; Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs; platform risks: failure mode: Credit denial or impermissible contingent-fee arrangement; trigger: Expired program authority, late certification, unsupported research expenses, or restricted practitioner compensation; impact: Reduced credits, amended returns, penalties, and fee repayment exposure; detection metric: Deadline exceptions, certification denials, and unsupported expense share; fallback: Exclude unsupported claims and use compliant fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review; id: solar_tax_equity_depreciation_strip_syndication; track id: track_1; name: Commercial Solar Tax-Equity Flip & Bonus-Depreciation Strip Syndication; mechanism: Arrange commercial solar partnership-flip investments that allocate supported tax benefits and cash flows to genuine equity owners; depreciation cannot be sold as a standalone credit, and allocations require economic substance, tax compliance, and securities-law review.; inputs: Solar project costs, ownership records, and operating contracts; Investor tax capacity and dated depreciation eligibility analysis; Counsel-reviewed partnership waterfall and securities offering documents; workflow: 1. Underwrite project cash flows, eligible basis, construction and service dates, and current credit and depreciation availability; 2. Verify investor suitability, tax capacity, at-risk and passive-loss limits, and applicable securities and intermediary requirements; 3. Structure counsel-approved partnership allocations and flip terms with genuine equity risk, basis adjustments, and recapture protections; 4. Close through authorized intermediaries and monitor operations, tax reporting, and flip conditions before distributing permitted fees; metrics: Qualified tax-equity capital closed; Realized investor distributions versus underwritten waterfall; Net permitted placement fees after legal and diligence costs; platform risks: failure mode: Tax allocations disallowed or unlicensed securities placement; trigger: Unsupported depreciation stripping, inadequate economic substance, ineligible project timing, or unauthorized transaction-based compensation; impact: Tax assessments, recapture, investor losses, and fee disgorgement exposure; detection metric: Unresolved tax opinion conditions and securities compliance exceptions; fallback: Suspend solicitation and closing, use appropriately licensed intermediaries, and restructure only as independently reviewed genuine equity ownership; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold; trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules; impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle; detection metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance; fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required; play id: distressed_asset_recovery; fallback: Never inject hidden tracking or background ad scripts; keep existing permissions narrow, grandfather all legacy free features, and monetize strictly via additive Pro workflows; play id: expired_chrome_extension_acquisitions;
